candidates.rationale: Opens with the practical failure case: a SWE-bench coding task where hierarchical orchestration nails the planning phase but collapses during debugging because the task structure shifted from decomposable to iterative. This concrete failure motivates the entire paper and makes the contribution feel necessary. The problem-first frame resonates with practitioners who have watched their multi-agent pipelines succeed on one phase and fail on the next.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.argumentation_note: Open with a concrete SWE-bench task showing phase transition: planning (high-D) succeeds under hierarchy, debugging (high-I) fails under same hierarchy. Quantify the cost of static assignment. State hypothesis and four contributions: (1) D-I-T feature extractor from execution traces, (2) phase boundary detection, (3) contextual bandit switching policy, (4) shared state transfer protocol.

candidates.rationale: Opens with the theoretical insight that orchestration topologies encode implicit structural priors about tasks, formalizable as distributions in D-I-T space. When a task trajectory crosses a topology boundary, the system should switch. Formally rigorous framing that appeals to theory-oriented NeurIPS reviewers, but risks losing practitioners.
